goal: A messy real-world export still imports. Values written in a form the catalogue would reject are normalized on the way in where their meaning is recoverable, kept rather than discarded where it is not, and an entry is refused only when there is nothing left to build a record from.
read_first: specs/004-import-references-bibtex/spec.md — User Story 2, FR-017 through FR-021, FR-029, SC-002, and the Refinements section
specs/004-import-references-bibtex/plan.md — Design in brief, especially where cleaning sits relative to mapping
specs/004-import-references-bibtex/research.md — what bibtexparser gives us, including latexenc.latex_to_unicode
specs/004-import-references-bibtex/decisions.md — D1 (recovery before rejection, the maintainer's own framing), D11, D12, D13 (where you may preserve a value you cannot rescue)
specs/004-import-references-bibtex/progress.md — the tail, for what US1 already built
literature/importers/bibtex.py — US1's mapping, which you extend rather than replace
tests/test_importers/test_bibtex.py — the single test module for this format; add classes, change nothing existing
literature/converters.py — from_csl_json and the validation that decides what the catalogue accepts; do not change it
literature/models.py — ItemDate.literal and ItemDate.raw, the existing fallback for a date that cannot be structured

tasks.description: Write TestCleaning: a DOI written as a resolver URL (https://doi.org/10.x/y) or carrying a doi: label normalizes to the bare identifier (FR-017); LaTeX escapes decode to the characters they represent and capitalization-protecting braces are removed, while a construct the decoder does not recognise is left as it stands rather than dropped (FR-018). Fixtures doi_as_url.bib, doi_labelled.bib and latex_escapes.bib exist for this.

Write TestRecovery: a value that cannot be normalized into something the catalogue accepts is preserved instead of failing its entry (FR-019); an unresolvable date goes to the record's existing fallback (FR-020, fixture unparseable_date.bib); an entry is reported as failed only where it cannot be parsed or the catalogue rejects it after recovery (FR-021).

Add the cleaning helpers to literature/importers/bibtex.py: LaTeX decoding through bibtexparser.latexenc.latex_to_unicode, brace stripping, and per-field normalization for DOI and ISBN. Nothing in them may evaluate their input (FR-029, Article V). Turns T021 green.

Wire cleaning into to_csl_json ahead of mapping, and route a value that survives cleaning but still will not validate into preservation rather than failure, per D13 — the narrow per-field case only, never the general sweep, which is US4. Turns T022 green.
Assert against the whole committed corpus that no entry is refused for a reason normalization resolves, and that every refusal carries a reason naming what could not be recovered (SC-002).

acceptance: doi_as_url.bib and doi_labelled.bib import with the same stored DOI as the equivalent clean entry in clean_multi_type.bib.

latex_escapes.bib imports with accented and special characters as the characters themselves, brace-protected capitalization preserved as plain text without the braces, and any construct the decoder does not know left visible in the stored value rather than dropped.
unparseable_date.bib imports with the unresolvable date in ItemDate's existing fallback, and the entry is created rather than failed.
Across the whole corpus, no entry is refused for a reason normalization resolves, and every refusal names what could not be recovered.
The full suite stays green and coverage floors hold (project 90%, patch 85%).
prohibitions: Do not modify or delete any test you did not author in this story. test_bibtex.py already holds US1's classes; add yours alongside them. If a pre-existing test genuinely must change, mark the task blocked and say why in concerns.

Do not change literature/converters.py. The contract requires from_csl_json's behaviour to be unchanged for existing callers. If a value only validates by changing it, that is a signal to clean the value, not to relax the validator.
Do not change the contract's workflow in literature/importers/base.py. Report it as a concern instead if you believe it is wrong.
Do not implement BibLaTeX field or type names — US3, issue #32.
Do not build the general preservation of unmapped fields into CSL custom — US4, issue #33. D13 defines exactly how far you may go: one field at a time, at the point its own validation fails.
Do not add a runtime dependency. bibtexparser is already declared and carries the LaTeX decoder.
Nothing may evaluate file content. No eval, no exec, no shelling out, no subprocess, no network. A .bib file is untrusted input (FR-029, Article V).
No GitHub operations: you hold no tokens. No network beyond the package registry.
conventions: Test-first, Article I: write the failing test, confirm it fails for the right reason, then implement minimally to green.
One test module, tests/test_importers/test_bibtex.py, concerns grouped by class. Do not split it into a package — the constitution requires test modules to mirror the literature/ tree.
One source module, literature/importers/bibtex.py. The maintainer rejected splitting it at the plan gate; do not reintroduce a split on a prediction about size.
Article VIII: every human-readable string translatable, gettext_lazy for anything evaluated at import time.
Commit per task with the task id in the subject, e.g. 'T023: DOI normalization and LaTeX decoding'.
Append a progress.md entry per task: Did / Verified (commands and counts) / Next / Watch. Non-obvious choices go to decisions.md as Decision / Why / Revisit if.
Run the repo's full commit-hook chain, not just ruff — US1 shipped a lint failure because ruff does not look at .bib files. `poetry run pre-commit run --all-files` is the check that matches CI.

rituals.baseline: poetry run pytest -q --no-cov  (expect 585 passed before you start)
rituals.verify: poetry run pytest -q --no-cov && poetry run pre-commit run --all-files && poetry run mypy literature && poetry run deptry .

report: Return JSON per kit/schemas/completion-report.schema.json: per-task status with evidence (tests added, exact commands run, exit codes), commits, deviations with decisions.md references, concerns, and any blocked tasks. Report what you ran, not what you believe — every claim is re-verified independently.
